skills.name: Matched Grip
skills.description: The standard grip where both hands hold the stick the same way, palms facing down.

skills.name: Traditional Grip
skills.description: Jazz-originated grip where the left hand holds the stick underhand.

skills.name: Posture & Throne Height
skills.description: Proper seated posture and drum throne height for relaxed, injury-free playing.

skills.name: Basic Hi-Hat Foot Technique
skills.description: Using the hi-hat pedal to open and close the cymbals with the left foot.

skills.name: Bass Drum Heel-Toe
skills.description: The heel-toe bass drum technique for smooth and controlled kick strokes.

skills.name: Single Stroke Roll
skills.description: The most fundamental rudiment: alternating single strokes RLRL.

skills.name: Double Stroke Roll
skills.description: Two strokes per hand: RRLL, the foundation of the drum roll.

skills.name: Single Paradiddle
skills.description: RLRR LRLL — the classic paradiddle sticking pattern.

skills.name: Flam
skills.description: A grace note played just before the main stroke for a fuller sound.

skills.name: Reading Basic Notation
skills.description: Reading standard drum notation: note values, rests, and time signatures.

skills.name: 4/4 Time Signature
skills.description: Understanding 4/4 common time: counting beats, bar lines, and subdivision.

skills.name: Basic Rock Beat
skills.description: The fundamental rock groove: bass on 1 & 3, snare on 2 & 4, eighth-note hi-hats.

skills.name: Basic Hi-Hat Variations
skills.description: Varying the hi-hat pattern: open hi-hats on the 'and' beats, sixteenth notes.

skills.name: Basic Coordination
skills.description: Playing hands and feet independently: hands on a rhythm while feet keep a simple pattern.

skills.name: Eighth-Note Triplet Feel
skills.description: Playing a swung, triplet-based groove for blues and jazz contexts.

skills.name: Double Paradiddle
skills.description: RLRLRR LRLRLL — an extended paradiddle sticking.

skills.name: Linear Drumming
skills.description: No two limbs play at the same time — every beat is voiced by a single limb.

skills.name: Ghost Notes
skills.description: Very soft snare strokes played between the main backbeat to add texture and feel.

skills.name: Polyrhythm 3 over 4
skills.description: Superimposing three equal divisions over a four-beat bar.

skills.name: Odd Time Signatures
skills.description: Playing confidently in 5/4, 7/8, 7/4 and other asymmetric meters.

skills.name: Brushwork Basics
skills.description: Using drum brushes for swirling and sweeping sounds on the snare drum.

skills.name: Heel-Up Bass Drum Technique
skills.description: Driving the beater with the ball of the foot lifted, enabling more power and speed.

skills.name: Funk Groove
skills.description: Sixteenth-note hi-hat groove with syncopated bass drum and ghost-note snare.

skills.name: Jazz Ride Pattern
skills.description: The classic jazz ride cymbal comping pattern with swung eighth notes.

skills.name: One-Handed Roll (Moeller)
skills.description: The Moeller whip-stroke technique for fast, relaxed single-handed rolls.

skills.name: Drum Fill Construction
skills.description: Building musical fills around the kit — transitions, tom patterns, and endings.

skills.name: Press Roll
skills.description: The closed (buzz) roll using sustained pressure strokes to create a continuous sound.

skills.name: Advanced Polyrhythm
skills.description: Simultaneous independent limb cycles: e.g. 4 against 3 against 2 across all four limbs.

skills.name: Metric Modulation
skills.description: Smoothly shifting perceived tempo by reinterpreting subdivisions as the new pulse.

skills.name: Double Bass Drumming
skills.description: Using two bass drums or a double pedal for fast alternating kick patterns.

skills.name: Orchestral Snare Technique
skills.description: Concert-level snare drumming: dynamics, rolls, and control for classical performance.

exercises.name: Grip & Posture Check
exercises.description: Sit at the kit and establish a relaxed matched grip. Check throne height — thighs slightly angled down.
exercises.notes: Focus on relaxed wrists. No tension in forearms.

exercises.name: Traditional Grip Introduction
exercises.description: Practice the left-hand traditional grip hold. Rotate forearm, nestle stick in the pocket between thumb and index.
exercises.notes: Use a pillow pad before moving to the kit.

exercises.name: Hi-Hat Foot Pulse
exercises.description: Tap quarter notes on the hi-hat pedal with your left foot while counting aloud.
exercises.notes: Keep tapping even and relaxed. Start with just the foot, no hands.

exercises.name: Bass Drum Single Strokes
exercises.description: Play single bass drum strokes at a steady tempo, focusing on consistent tone.
exercises.notes: Use heel-toe motion. Listen for a clean, full sound on each stroke.

exercises.name: Single Stroke Roll — Slow
exercises.description: RLRL at a slow tempo on the snare, focusing on even spacing and equal volume.
exercises.notes: Use a metronome. Each stroke should sound identical in volume.

exercises.name: Single Stroke Roll — Speed Build
exercises.description: Gradually increase tempo in 5 BPM increments, spending 2 minutes at each speed.
exercises.notes: Stop if tension appears. Speed comes from relaxation, not force.

exercises.name: Double Stroke — Open Roll
exercises.description: RRLL at a moderate tempo, keeping both strokes per hand even and controlled.
exercises.notes: The second stroke should be a rebound, not a separate arm movement.

exercises.name: Double Stroke Speed Drill
exercises.description: Practice doubles from 80 to 160 BPM using a 'slow-fast' approach.
exercises.notes: Allow the stick to do the work on the second stroke.

exercises.name: Single Paradiddle — Snare
exercises.description: RLRR LRLL on the snare at a comfortable tempo. Count aloud.
exercises.notes: Accent the first note of each group.

exercises.name: Paradiddle Around the Kit
exercises.description: Apply paradiddle sticking across the toms and snare to create a musical pattern.
exercises.notes: Move the accented notes to different drums.

exercises.name: Flam — Basic Approach
exercises.description: Practice single flams on the snare, alternating lead hands.
exercises.notes: The grace note should be very quiet — a whisper before the main stroke.

exercises.name: Reading Notation Worksheet
exercises.description: Read and clap/tap the rhythms in a beginner notation worksheet (quarter, half, whole notes).
exercises.notes: Count aloud: '1, 2, 3, 4' while tapping.

exercises.name: Counting in 4/4
exercises.description: Clap a written rhythm in 4/4, subdividing into eighth notes while counting.
exercises.notes: Say '1-and-2-and-3-and-4-and' aloud.

exercises.name: Basic Rock Beat — Introduction
exercises.description: Bass on 1 & 3, snare on 2 & 4, eighth-note hi-hats. Play for 5-minute blocks.
exercises.notes: Build it in layers: hi-hats first, then add snare, then bass.

exercises.name: Rock Beat — Tempo Range
exercises.description: Play the basic rock beat across a range from 70 to 130 BPM.
exercises.notes: The goal is comfort and consistency across tempos.

exercises.name: Open Hi-Hat on the 'and'
exercises.description: Add an open hi-hat on the 'and' of beat 2 or 4 to the basic rock beat.
exercises.notes: Close the hi-hat cleanly on the following downbeat.

exercises.name: Hands vs. Feet Independence
exercises.description: Play a quarter-note hand pattern while maintaining a separate foot ostinato.
exercises.notes: Start slowly. Let each limb be 'on autopilot' before adding complexity.

exercises.name: Shuffle Groove
exercises.description: Play a swung eighth-note groove (shuffle) in a 12-bar blues form.
exercises.notes: Listen to classic blues drummers for feel reference.

exercises.name: Double Paradiddle Drill
exercises.description: RLRLRR LRLRLL at a steady tempo on the snare.
exercises.notes: Watch for the doubled stroke at the end — keep it even.

exercises.name: Linear Groove Pattern 1
exercises.description: Play a classic funk linear pattern where kick, snare, and hi-hat never overlap.
exercises.notes: Visualise the pattern written on paper first.

exercises.name: Ghost Note Groove
exercises.description: Add ghost notes to a basic rock beat — quiet snare strokes on the 'e' and 'a' subdivisions.
exercises.notes: Ghost notes should be nearly inaudible — feel them more than hear them.

exercises.name: 3 over 4 Exercise
exercises.description: Play three equal strokes over a 4/4 bar on a practice pad, using a metronome.
exercises.notes: Tap foot on beat, hands on the triplet subdivision.

exercises.name: 5/4 Groove
exercises.description: Play a groove pattern in 5/4 time. Try grouping as 3+2 or 2+3.
exercises.notes: Count '1-2-3-4-5' aloud until it feels natural.

exercises.name: Brush Sweeping on Snare
exercises.description: Practice circular and sweeping brush motions on a snare with a snare head.
exercises.notes: Keep brushes flat on the head. Listen for a smooth, continuous sound.

exercises.name: Heel-Up Single Strokes
exercises.description: Heel-up bass drum singles at increasing tempos, focusing on ankle drive.
exercises.notes: Keep the leg relaxed. Drive from the ankle, not the thigh.

exercises.name: Funk Groove — Sixteenth Hi-Hats
exercises.description: Play a funk groove with sixteenth-note hi-hats, ghost notes on snare, and syncopated kick.
exercises.notes: Classic funk feel — think James Brown-era grooves.

exercises.name: Jazz Comping — Ride Pattern
exercises.description: Play the jazz ride pattern (dotted-eighth + sixteenth on ride), with hi-hat on 2 & 4.
exercises.notes: Keep the pattern loose and swinging. The ride should 'float'.

exercises.name: Basic Tom Fill Patterns
exercises.description: Play common 4-beat fills moving from high to low toms, using paradiddle sticking.
exercises.notes: Record yourself to evaluate evenness and timing.

exercises.name: Press Roll — Buzz Practice
exercises.description: Practice sustained press/buzz rolls on a snare, controlling the pressure for even sound.
exercises.notes: Use a practice pad. Apply downward pressure after each stroke.

exercises.name: Double Bass — Alternating Singles
exercises.description: Play alternating right-left single strokes on double bass pedal at varying tempos.
exercises.notes: Start at 60 BPM. Only increase when perfectly even.
